content.title: About
content.content: The chicken and cheese burrito is a Mexican dish consisting of a large wheat tortilla wrapped around a filling of tender chicken breast, melted cheese, rice, beans, and spices. It combines aromatic seasonings, protein, and carbohydrates for a balanced meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico where wheat flour is more common than corn.
Traditional fillings include black beans, but modern versions often use pinto or red beans.
There are countless variations, from beef and pork to vegetarian options with tofu or vegetables.
Burritos are commonly served with salsa, guacamole, and sour cream for added freshness and creaminess.
In the United States, burritos have become a fast‑food staple, found in chain restaurants and street carts.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: B vitamins
items.content: Chicken and whole‑grain tortilla supply B6 and B12 vitamins, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Provides fiber
items.content: Beans and rice contribute dietary fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: Energy‑dense
items.content: The mix of carbs and protein offers sustained satiety and energy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese and prepared sauces can be salty, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric load
items.content: Burritos are calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Food‑borne bacteria risk
items.content: Chicken must be cooked thoroughly to prevent salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Burritos are hand‑held; slice them in half for easier handling. Warm in a microwave or skillet to melt the cheese. Add fresh salsa, guacamole, or a squeeze of lime for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burrito in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze and reheat before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Candy is a popular chewy fruit‑flavored candy produced by NFS. It is known for its soft texture, bright packaging, and a range of flavors such as strawberry, orange, grape, and lime.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Candy first hit the market in the early 1990s and quickly became a favorite thanks to its unique taste‑and‑chew combination.
Each pack contains 12 individually wrapped pieces, each coated with a light sugar glaze.
The formula uses natural flavorings and food‑grade colourings approved by European regulators.
Candy is often given as a small treat at children’s parties and in school lunchboxes.
In 2022 NFS released a limited‑edition line enriched with vitamin C.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The sugar in the candy provides a quick boost of glucose, delivering an immediate energy lift.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: The limited edition is fortified with vitamin C, which supports immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Sweet taste stimulates serotonin release, helping to improve mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption may lead to weight gain, tooth decay, and blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: May contain trace amounts of nuts, soy, or gluten, which should be considered by people with allergies.

items.title: Not for children under 3
items.content: Small pieces can pose a choking hazard for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Candy is convenient to eat straight from the pack, use as a garnish for desserts, stir into ice cream, or incorporate into baked goods for a fruity boost.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place with the package tightly sealed. For longer shelf life, keep in the refrigerator to prevent the glaze from melting.

chicken-or-turkey-rice-and-vegetables-in.title: Chicken or Turkey with Rice and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of chicken or turkey meat, boiled rice and vegetables (carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens). It is served with a cream, white, or mushroom sauce. This provides a balanced source of protein, complex carbohydrates and vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are among the most widely consumed meats worldwide.
Rice is the primary energy source for more than half of the global population.
Broccoli is rich in vitamin C and compounds that support detoxification.
Dark‑green leafy vegetables (spinach, kale) contain high amounts of iron and folate.
Mushroom sauce adds umami flavor and provides beta‑glucans that benefit immunity.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Poultry meat supplies all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: Rice delivers glucose, sustaining energy levels over a prolonged period.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Vegetables contribute vitamins A, C, K and minerals such as potassium and magnesium, supporting heart and nerve function.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Fiber from vegetables and whole‑grain rice promotes healthy bowel movement.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Broccoli and leafy greens contain flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken or turkey proteins.

items.title: Sodium in sauces
items.content: Cream and white sauces often contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked poultry can harbor Salmonella; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of vegetables may cause gas in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, mixing meat, rice and vegetables in roughly equal parts. Drizzle the chosen sauce over the top or serve it on the side. Fresh herbs such as parsley or dill can be added for extra aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat to at least 75 °C before serving. Keep the sauce separate to prevent the rice from becoming soggy.

content.title: About
content.content: Decaffeinated cafe con leche coffee is a milk‑based coffee drink made from roasted beans that have had the caffeine removed and whole milk. It offers a smooth, creamy flavor with a hint of sweetness and roasted coffee aroma, but without the stimulating effect.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeination is usually done by Swiss‑water or CO₂ extraction, preserving most aromatic compounds.
The term “cafe con leche” is Spanish for “coffee with milk.”
In Spain and Latin America the drink is often served in large cups, sometimes topped with cinnamon or vanilla.
Decaf coffee may still contain up to 0.1 % caffeine, which is considered safe for most sensitive individuals.
The antioxidant content in decaf coffee is nearly identical to regular coffee thanks to retained chlorogenic acids.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee provides chlorogenic acids and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Milk supplies calcium and protein, while coffee stimulates gastric juice production.

items.title: May lower risk of certain diseases
items.content: Regular moderate coffee consumption is linked to reduced risk of type 2 diabetes and some neurodegenerative disorders.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Coffee contains niacin (B3) and riboflavin (B2), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing aroma
items.content: Even without caffeine, the scent and taste can have a calming, mood‑lifting effect.

items.title: Milk allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People with dairy sensitivities should choose a non‑dairy alternative.

items.title: Residual caffeine
items.content: Highly caffeine‑sensitive individuals may still react to trace amounts.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee can increase stomach acidity, which may aggravate gastritis or reflux.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Some decaf products contain flavor enhancers; always check the ingredient list.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, optionally adding cinnamon, vanilla, or a small amount of sugar. For a cold version, chill the drink and serve over ice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the package in a dry, cool place away from direct light. Once opened, use within 2–3 weeks to preserve flavor.

content.title: About
content.content: Fajita is a ready‑to‑use spice blend created by NFS for preparing the Mexican dish “fajita”. The mix includes dried chilies, paprika, garlic, onion and aromatic herbs that give meat, fish or vegetables a characteristic spicy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “fajita” comes from the Spanish word meaning “strip” or “ribbon”, referring to the traditional cut of meat.
The NFS blend is formulated to balance heat and aroma, making it suitable for both classic and modern recipes.
The product contains no artificial colours or preservatives.
Fajita NFS is suitable for home cooking as well as professional restaurant use.
One package is designed for 30‑50 servings, depending on the amount of protein used.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: The blend contains paprika and dried chilies, which are high in vitamins C and E, helping protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Cumin and garlic stimulate gastric juice production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: No added sugars are present, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: The blend can be hot; people with sensitive stomachs should use it sparingly.

items.title: Allergy to spices
items.content: Contains garlic and cumin, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The mix includes salt; those limiting sodium intake should account for it in their overall diet.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add 1‑2 teaspoons of the blend to 500 g of meat, fish or vegetables, and sauté over high heat until a golden crust forms. It can also be used in marinades, sauces and soups to boost flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the packet in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, seal tightly to preserve aroma. Shelf life is indicated on the label.

pizza-with-meat-other-than-pepperoni-fro.title: Frozen Thin‑Crust Pizza with Meat (no pepperoni)

content.title: About
content.content: This is a frozen pizza with a thin, crispy crust topped with a variety of meats (such as ham, beef, chicken), tomato sauce and cheese. It is designed for quick oven preparation and retains the flavor and juiciness of the meat after heating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thin crust gives a crunchier bite compared with traditional thick crusts.
Frozen pizzas can be stored up to 12 months at –18 °C.
Meat blends without pepperoni often include smoked ham, ground beef and chicken pieces.
The tomato sauce is usually made from ripe tomatoes, basil and oregano.
This pizza is ideal for fast lunches or dinners that require minimal preparation.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef and chicken contain iron that supports normal blood formation.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Cheese adds a good amount of calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and tomato sauce are rich in vitamins B6 and B12, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: When properly heated, the pizza retains nutrients and is easy on the stomach.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ready‑made pizza often contains a lot of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Cheese and meat can increase saturated fat intake, a concern for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger reactions in people allergic to lactose or casein.

items.title: Needs thorough heating
items.content: Insufficiently heated pizza may harbor live bacteria, especially if it was not frozen properly.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The thin crust contains gluten, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Preheat the oven to 200 °C and bake the pizza for 10–12 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling. Serve hot; optionally garnish with fresh basil or arugula for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen pizza in a freezer at –18 °C or lower. After thawing (if required), consume within 24 hours and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Plain popped potato chips are light, crunchy slices of potato created by rapid heating that causes the pieces to “pop” without the addition of flavorings or salt. Their neutral taste makes them a versatile base for further seasoning.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Popped chips are produced by quickly heating potato pieces, causing moisture to vaporize and the slice to expand into a porous structure.
Unlike traditional fried chips, popped chips are made without oil, resulting in lower calorie density.
The first commercial popped chips appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
Their neutral flavor makes them popular for culinary experiments, allowing home cooks to add custom spices and sauces.
In some markets, popped chips are sold in airtight “food‑aerosol” packaging to preserve crunch.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Because no oil is used during production, popped chips contain far less fat than conventional fried chips.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potato provides starch, delivering a quick source of energy.

items.title: Vitamin C presence
items.content: A small amount of vitamin C survives the popping process, supporting immune function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The chips retain some fiber, which aids normal digestion.

items.title: Low sodium (when unsalted)
items.content: Unsalted versions are suitable for people monitoring their sodium intake.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A minority of individuals may be allergic to potato, experiencing skin or gastrointestinal reactions.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes have a high glycemic index, so large portions can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Storage contamination
items.content: Improper storage can allow moisture to enter, leading to mold growth.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Some manufacturers add anti‑oxidants or preservatives; check the label if you are sensitive to additives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Popped potato chips can be enjoyed straight from the bag or used as a crunchy base for homemade seasonings: sprinkle with paprika, cheese powder, herbs, or add to salads for texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the chips in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from light. Properly stored, they stay crisp for 3–4 weeks. Discard if they become damp or develop a stale, off‑flavor.

content.title: About
content.content: Sherbet is a refreshing frozen dessert made from fruit puree, sugar, and sometimes dairy. The “all flavors” version combines more than 20 classic tastes such as lemon, raspberry, orange, mango, and strawberry in one package.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sherbet has a history of over 200 years and originates from the Middle East, where it was made from fruit juices and honey.
Unlike ice cream, traditional sherbet contains no butter, making it lighter and less caloric.
Modern versions are often fortified with vitamins C and B6, as well as probiotics.
In Russia, sherbet’s popularity surged in the 1990s after the arrival of imported brands.
Sherbet can be served as a standalone dessert or used in cocktails and fruit salads.

items.title: Rich in Vitamin C
items.content: Fruit components provide a high level of vitamin C, supporting immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low Fat Content
items.content: The absence of butter makes sherbet less fatty compared to ice cream, suitable for diet-conscious eating.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Its high water content helps maintain fluid balance, especially in hot weather.

items.title: Source of Minerals
items.content: Fruit ingredients supply potassium and magnesium, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Digestive Support
items.content: Some flavors include natural probiotics that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Sugar
items.content: Sherbet contains a notable amount of sugar, so people with diabetes should limit consumption.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Certain variants may contain dairy, nuts, or gluten, requiring caution for those with allergies.

items.title: Crystallization
items.content: Improper storage can lead to crystal formation, affecting texture.

items.title: Cold Sensitivity
items.content: Excessive intake of very cold dessert may cause discomfort for individuals sensitive to cold.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve sherbet in individual cups or cones, optionally topped with fresh berries, mint, or a drizzle of fruit sauce. Let it sit at room temperature for 2‑3 minutes before serving to enhance aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep sherbet in a freezer at –18 °C in its original packaging. After opening, transfer to an airtight container to prevent absorption of other odors. If thawed, use within 24 hours.
